A 50-year-old male was suffering from pneumonia and the physician prescribed cotrimoxazole. Cotrimoxazole contains sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim as a fixed-dose combination. Which of the following is FALSE regarding the Fixed dose combination?

options.label: B
options.text: Side effect of one component cannot be counteracted by other

options.label: C
options.text: Combined formulation ensures that a single drug will not be administered eg. Tuberculosis

questions.answerText: Side effect of one component cannot be counteracted by other
questions.solutionHtml:
Side effect of one component cannot be counteracted by other

FDC:

  • Convenient and better patient compliance
  • Side effects of one component may be counteracted by another; eg. A thiazide plus spironolactone
  • Certain Drug combinations are synergistic. Eg. Levodopa and carbidopa
  • The combined formulation ensures that a single drug will not be administered eg. Tuberculosis and HIV

questions.stem: A pharmaceutical drug company manufacturer labels the drug containing 10 mg of levocetirizine. On subsequent analysis by the government, it shows that only 5mg of the drug was present. What type of drug it is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Spurious drug
  • In this scenario, there is a decreased dose of the active ingredient of a drug, so it is called a spurious drug or counterfeit drug


Drugs and cosmetics act 1945

questions.stem: Which of the following is irrational Fixed dose combinations banned in India?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nimesulide + diclofenac
  • Nimesulide caused liver failure. Hence, the combination of paracetamol and nimesulide was banned in India due to the high risk of hepatotoxicity
  • Levodopa + carbidopa – beneficial FDC
  • Isoniazid + rifampicin – for latent tuberculosis
  • Ibuprofen + paracetamol - for pain relief and fever
